subject: Genetics
title: The White House Announcement
description: A micro-lesson that makes The White House Announcement usable.

hook.text: On June 26, 2000, Clinton stood with Collins and Venter. Rivals side by side. The genome draft was done.

buildup.text: Clinton compared it to Meriwether Lewis unrolling the map of the continent. A new frontier had been charted.

discovery.text: The announcement was carefully staged—both teams declared victory simultaneously. Neither would stand second.

twist.text: The genome wasn't actually finished. The 'draft' was 90% complete with thousands of gaps. Marketing beat science.

climax.text: The real completion came quietly in 2003—no press conference, no president. The gaps took three more years.

punchline.text: The headline came first. The science finished later.

quiz.question: When was the draft human genome announced at the White House?
